name: Ninety-Nine (adding game)
description: 99 (adding game): play cards to a central pile; A=1 or 11, 2-9=face, 10=-10, J/Q=0, K=99 or reset. Avoid exceeding 99; first to push over loses. Similar to 98. USA/UK.

overview.description: 99 (adding game): play cards to a central pile; A=1 or 11, 2-9=face, 10=-10, J/Q=0, K=99 or reset. Avoid exceeding 99; first to push over loses. Similar to 98. USA/UK.

history.origins:
Origin: USA and United Kingdom
Historical development: The game has evolved over time in its regions of origin.
Cultural significance: 99 holds cultural importance in both the USA and the UK.
timeline: Mid 20th century: Families in North America report playing 99 as an adding game closely related to 98 and One Hundred.
Late 20th century: 99 is documented on major card-game reference sites as a casual adding and drinking game in both the USA and the UK.

setup.deck:
Deck type: 52 cards
Card rankings: Standard (Ace high or low depending on variant)
setup.dealing: Cards dealt to reach 99 points or closest without busting.

rules.objective: Avoid being the player who pushes the total over 99.
rules.gameplay: Play one card; add value to pile (A=1/11, 10=-10, K=99 or 0, etc.). Announce total; over 99 loses.
keyRules: A=1 or 11, 2-9=face value, 10=-10, J/Q=0, K=99 or reset
Play one card per turn; announce new total

strategy.basic: Save K to reset; use 10 when total is high.
